title: Zadok and Abiathar
lead: The two chief priests under David. Abiathar, the last of Eli's line, backed Adonijah and was banished to Anathoth; Zadok anointed Solomon, and his descendants held the high priesthood in Jerusalem until the second century BC.

sections.h: Zadok and Abiathar across the Bible
sections.b: Abiathar son of Ahimelech is the only priest to escape Saul's massacre at Nob, and he brings the ephod to David in the wilderness (1 Samuel 22:20–23; 1 Samuel 23:6). Zadok son of Ahitub first appears in Samuel as one of David's priests in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 8:17, where the Hebrew names "Ahimelech son of Abiathar" beside him, probably a slip for "Abiathar son of Ahimelech"); Chronicles places a young warrior named Zadok with David at Hebron (1 Chronicles 12:28). Both carry the ark out of the city when David flees Absalom and stay as his informers (2 Samuel 15:24–36). In the succession crisis Abiathar backs Adonijah and Zadok anoints Solomon; Abiathar is banished to Anathoth (1 Kings 1:7–8, 1:39; 1 Kings 2:26–27, 2:35). Chronicles traces Zadok to Aaron through Eleazar (1 Chronicles 6:3–8, 6:50–53). Ezekiel gives the sons of Zadok sole charge of the altar because they stayed faithful (Ezekiel 40:46; Ezekiel 44:15), and the Zadokite line held the high priesthood until the crisis of the 170s BC. The Sadducees' name may come from Zadok, and the Dead Sea Scrolls speak of "the sons of Zadok" as the community's priests.
